findings.wentWrong: Very few scored more than two: fusion was confused with fission; 'atoms' were said to join rather than nuclei; that it happens naturally in the Sun and stars was sometimes recalled; the main by-product (helium) was rarely given, with 'energy' the usual wrong answer.
findings.rule: Two light nuclei join to make a heavier nucleus (helium) and release energy.

findings.asked: The same fusion QWC at Higher.
findings.wentWrong: Most found it hard: what happens to the nuclei was not explained, the release of energy was left out, and energy was again offered as the by-product.
findings.rule: Say nuclei, say join, say energy released, say helium.

ruleToRemember: Fusion: two light (hydrogen) nuclei join at very high temperature and pressure to form a heavier helium nucleus, releasing a large amount of energy; it powers the Sun and stars, and it is hard to achieve on Earth. Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus - the opposite.
aStarSignal: A fusion QWC that contrasts it with fission, names the conditions, the product and the energy, and mentions why it is not yet a practical power source.
